# Air Scrubber The air scrubber is essential for keeping the atmosphere free of waste gases released by living creatures or produced by atmospheric incidents. Its primary function is to remove unwanted gases from the surrounding atmosphere.
An air scrubber requires [textlink="power" link="Power"] from a nearby [textlink="LV cable" link="VoltageNetworks"] to operate.
By default, the air scrubber removes every gas except nitrogen and oxygen from the surrounding atmosphere. It will continue operating this way until a [textlink="linked" link="Networking"] [textlink="air alarm" link="AirAlarms"] assigns it a different mode.
You can weld an air scrubber with any welding tool to stop it from operating.
## Configuration When [textlink="linked" link="Networking"] to an [textlink="air alarm" link="AirAlarms"], air scrubbers gain additional functionality.
Choose which gases to remove from the "Gas filters" drop-down list. Keep in mind that this selection resets whenever the [textlink="air alarm's" link="AirAlarms"] mode changes.
Air scrubbers have two direction settings: Scrubbing and Siphoning. - Scrubbing removes gases according to the selected filters. - Siphoning ignores every filter and draws all gases out of the atmosphere.
Both modes are limited by the Rate setting, which specifies in liters how quickly the scrubber draws gases from the surrounding atmosphere.
Air scrubbers also have a WideNet setting that extends their operating radius. Normally, a scrubber cleans only the atmosphere on its own tile. In WideNet mode, the scrubber cleans gas from the 4 tiles around it, as shown below:
This effectively multiplies the total rate because the scrubber begins working on 5 tiles at once.
Scrubbers [textlink="linked" link="Networking"] to an [textlink="air alarm" link="AirAlarms"] in automatic mode will automatically enable WideNet through the [textlink="air alarm's" link="AirAlarms"] "Filtering (Wide)" mode when a high concentration of unwanted gases is detected in the atmosphere.
WideNet is extremely useful for quickly removing large quantities of tritium from plasma burn chambers.
